# Benny Labs Foundation

> Benny Labs Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit for research, invention and public education. Site: https://bennylabs.org/

## AI research: AI in its Infancy
- [AI in its Infancy](https://bennylabs.org/ai-in-its-infancy/): the foundation's project on making AI models reach the same answer with less computation, tested with pass lines written before each run.
- [Paper 1, plain Markdown](https://bennylabs.org/ai-in-its-infancy/paper.md): "When a Warm Cache Changes the Answer in Reduced-Depth Inference" by Benny Goldstein and Eytan Yair Goldstein, November 21, 2026. Shows that a document-only layer-skipping plan served through a prefix cache on a hybrid model (Qwen3.8-27B in vLLM) gives outputs that depend on whether the cache is warm, that aligning to a 16-token block does not fix it because the engine resumes only every 784 tokens, and that aligning to 784 or re-applying the plan on every request gives exact agreement on 240 of 240 follow-ups. No speed saving is claimed.

## Traffic research: Transactional Traffic Mediator
- [Transactional Traffic Mediator](https://bennylabs.org/transactional-traffic/): a patent-pending coordination layer for lane-level cooperation between vehicles.
- [Working paper](https://bennylabs.org/transactional-traffic/paper/): "Verified Cooperation as a Traffic Resource: Sensor-Verified Multi-Vehicle Corridors and Verification-Gated Token Settlement" by Benny Goldstein, November 25, 2026. Describes lane-level localization by sensor fusion and radio ranging, a plan in which two or more vehicles each perform a different micro-maneuver to open one corridor, verification by before-and-after gap measurement with witnessed distance bounding, and tokens credited only on verification and settled in one netted batch per period. A design and analysis paper; no field trial is reported.
- [ThermalCore working paper](https://bennylabs.org/thermalcore/paper/): "The Heating Element That Computes: An Immersion Computing Module for the Standard Water-Heater Element Port" by Benny Goldstein, November 25, 2026. Describes a sealed computing module that fits the standard heating-element port of a water heater, shows that the port-limited power matches a household's average water-heating load, and gives a lumped thermal model in which the coupling between dies and enclosure wall, not the water side, limits power. A design and analysis paper; no prototype has been measured.
- [Worm Cargo working paper](https://bennylabs.org/worm-cargo/paper/): "The Sorting Hub That Drives: Routing Packages Through a Coupled Chain of Autonomous Cargo Vehicles" by Benny Goldstein, November 25, 2026. Describes driverless cargo vehicles that releasably couple into a live chain and route destination-addressed packages through one another, including across an intermediate vehicle, so parcels are sorted in motion or parked without a fixed hub. An open model finds the time saved is essentially hub dwell, that chain order changes transfers by about half, and that one coupling aperture (about 2,000 parcels an hour) and the shared road needed (about 20 km of coupling overhead plus the sort) are the main limits. A design and analysis paper; no prototype exists. Patent pending (U.S. Application No. 19/719,219).
- [Living Nails working paper](https://bennylabs.org/living-nails/paper/): "The Nail That Carries No Battery: Passive Fingernail Displays Powered and Driven Through Jewelry" by Benny Goldstein, November 25, 2026. Describes artificial nails that carry only a display and contacts, with no battery and no radio, powered and fed image data over a fine conductor (which can be a jewelry chain) from a ring, wrist band or linked rings. An open model finds one hand offers about 5 cm2 of display, a ring holds about 29 times and a bracelet about 286 times the energy of a cell that fits under a nail, and the conductor loses under 1%; it also finds a ring cannot keep five emissive nails lit all day, Bluetooth cannot stream video so animation must be stored in the hub, and addressable-LED daisy chains waste most of their power at idle. A design and analysis paper; no prototype exists. Patent pending (U.S. Application No. 19/724,868).
